video_title: Tom Dundon's Cheapness Hit's a New Low (Or High?) | Rachel Nichols and Chris Mannix

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Portland Trail Blazers seek $600 million in public funding for arena
quotes.excerpt: the team is looking for $600 million of public funding from the state, county and the city

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: We have had some developments in the ongoing saga with the Portland Trail Blazers. The team is looking for $600 million of public funding from the state, county and the city to remodel the Moda Center, which is 30 years old. Last week in Las Vegas, Adam Silver said that the negotiations between the city and the team have gone off track. This week, we have seen some reporting from Jason Quick of The Athletic that quotes a team source saying they are very far apart on an agreement on a deal like this. The Blazers, who are now led by Tom Dundon, have called that term sheet a non-starter.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: I would be pretty nervous, and I would be nervous not just from these latest developments, but the national media and the national fans have really started to have the temperature raise here. In Portland, they have been reporting on this for months. It just hasn't looked good.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: City ownership of the arena complicates the remodeling project
quotes.excerpt: the city owns the arena, and there are a lot of people out there that like, hey

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: One of the big issues with this arena is I think a little bit of a misunderstanding. The city owns the arena, and there are a lot of people out there that like, hey, if someone else, you were renting an apartment and they wanted you to completely remodel it, you wouldn't do that. You would think that was unfair, the owner should remodel it. The way the city owns the arena is that it was willed or gifted to the city as part of the sort of transition from the late Paul Allen's ownership to get to this point to sell the team and everything for a dollar. It was gifted to the city as part of the sort of transition from the late Paul Allen's ownership to get to this point to sell the team and everything for a dollar.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: Jody Allen and the Allen family did that.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Public funds should not subsidize billionaire-owned sports teams
quotes.excerpt: citizens should not be paying for sports stadiums, arenas, teams, especially now that they're all owned

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: The bottom line, no matter who you think is right or wrong, citizens should not be paying for sports stadiums, arenas, teams, especially now that they're all owned by billionaires. There may have been a time where the guy who owned the team was just a little bit richer than all the other rich people in town. When Jerry Buss bought the Lakers, he was a very successful commercial real estate developer. He was not a billionaire and never was a billionaire. When you have the gap in wealth between today's sports owners and how most people live day-to-day, it is obscene that we let any city, any municipality, any state, I believe the state of California has a law against this, of the city paying for the arena.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: I think the Moda Center is dumb, quite frankly. It really needs to be torn down.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Blazers' failure to disclose use of public funds is problematic
quotes.excerpt: they're still not willing to reveal what they would use the money for

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: The biggest issue I have with Tom Dundon and his team on this and this came from the Jason Quick story is that they're still not willing to reveal what they would use the money for. They've said they've got concepts of how they would improve the Moda Center. If you are asking for $600 million, you would have to articulate what you are going to use the money for. If the city and the county want to know what you are going to do with the money, you should be able to send them specs of everything that you were going to do.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: I will say this. When this initially bubbled up a couple months ago, I tweeted something about it because I feel very strongly that public money should not go toward billionaire welfare. I got the pushback because I pointed out that Oregon, I believe in the pre-K through 12th grade, is the 47th out of 50 states in the country in education.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA is nervous about the Portland Trail Blazers' future
quotes.excerpt: that tells me that the NBA is very nervous about the direction this goes

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: To hear Adam Silver, who is generally pretty optimistic about these things, very succinctly say that this has gone off track and point out that they basically assigned somebody to this in the league office and that person is covering it from day-to-day, that tells me that the NBA is very nervous about the direction this goes. And that tells me that there is probably a belief in the league office that this team packing up and moving is on the table.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: Will the ownership group in Memphis move? There are protective market situations.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Blazers ownership and city officials share blame for current standoff
quotes.excerpt: I think there's a blame pie. I don't think it's one or the other

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: I think there's a blame pie. I don't think it's one or the other. I don't think it's black or white. I think you would definitely blame the owner, the greedy billionaire for taking the team out of there because he didn't get exactly what he wanted. But I would also blame some of the city officials for letting it get to this point and allowing, as much as it sucks to put up money, losing the Trail Blazers would be such a massive loss for the city and the state.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: It's one of the biggest cities.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Tom Dundon's track record suggests he will get his deal
quotes.excerpt: I don't think Tom Dundon bought this team with an intention to move it out

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: I actually don't think that I don't think Tom Dundon bought this team with an intention to move it out. I just base that on that he bought the Carolina Hurricanes. People thought he was going to move that team. I think I think Dundon, and for better or worse, and a lot of times it's worse, I don't think he gives a bleep about what anybody thinks of him. I think he's going to get the deal that he wants, and if he doesn't get it, he's going to pick up his team and he's going to leave.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: And I know why that's not against the rules, it's not against the rules because the owners run the NBA.
